name: VCC2020
description: In this paper, we present the voice conversion (VC) systems developed at Nagoya University (NU) for the Voice Conversion Challenge 2020 (VCC2020). We aim to determine the effectiveness of two recent significant technologies in VC: sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models and autoregressive (AR) neural vocoders. Two respective systems were developed for the two tasks in the challenge: for task 1, we adopted the Voice Transformer Network, a Transformer-based seq2seq VC model, and extended it with synthetic parallel data to tackle nonparallel data; for task 2, we used the frame-based cyclic variational autoencoder (CycleVAE) to model the spectral features of a speech waveform and the AR WaveNet vocoder with additional fine-tuning. By comparing with the baseline systems, we confirmed that the seq2seq modeling can improve the conversion similarity and that the use of AR vocoders can improve the naturalness of the converted speech.
reputation: Voice Conversion Challenge benchmarks are a long-running and well-known evaluation setting in the speech conversion community.
notes: Typically evaluated with subjective listening tests such as similarity and naturalness MOS; results are challenge- and task-specific rather than a single universal score.
